query: What signals are linked to longer resolution duration values?

per_column.name: resolution_duration_seconds
per_column.rationale: This is the resolution duration itself expressed in seconds -- a direct restatement of the focus variable, not an external predictor.

per_column.name: resolution_duration_tier
per_column.rationale: A binned/discretized version of the focus duration (short/medium/long/very_long). It is a deterministic function of the outcome, not a predictor.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: Numeric encoding of priority, known at open time and plausibly correlated with how long resolution takes. Legitimate external predictor.

per_column.name: opened_hour
per_column.rationale: Hour of day the ticket was opened, known before resolution; can carry signal about staffing/load affecting duration.

per_column.name: is_off_hours_open
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket opened outside business hours, known at open time; plausibly linked to longer resolution due to reduced coverage.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_resolution_seconds
per_column.rationale: Average resolution time of the assignee is computed FROM the resolution duration outcomes (aggregating the focus variable itself), so it leaks the target rather than being an independent predictor.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_seconds
per_column.rationale: Category-level mean of the focus variable; a target-derived aggregate that leaks the outcome unless carefully out-of-fold constructed, which is not evidenced here.

per_column.name: is_high_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity flag derived from priority, known at open time and plausibly associated with resolution duration. Legitimate predictor (though near-constant here).

judge.rationale: Half the added columns fail the technical claim: resolution_duration_seconds and resolution_duration_tier are restatements/discretizations of the focus, and the two *_avg_resolution_seconds columns are target-derived aggregates that leak the outcome. The genuine external predictors -- priority_numeric, opened_hour, is_off_hours_open, is_high_severity -- are plausible but weak and largely redundant with existing priority/opened_at columns (is_high_severity is near-constant at 474/26 and overlaps priority_numeric). As a set they add only modest legitimate predictive leverage beyond the original table.
